newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile slams El Abra copper mine over acid leak.
newsitem.headline: Chile slams El Abra copper mine over acid leak.

text.p: Chilean Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky criticized the new El Abra copper mine for delays in reporting a leak of sulphuric acid into a nearby river, the second serious accident at the pit in the last four months.
"What disturbs me most is the delay by El Abra in informing the public and the regional authorities of the accident," said Teplizky.
Local authorities are carrying out tests to see if the acid has contaminated water used by local Indian communities for their crops, said Teplizky.
El Abra, which is 51-percent owned by Cyprus Minerals, with 49 percent held by state copper giant Codelco, said it would issue a statement later Friday.

Influential local newspaper El Mercurio, which splashed the story on its front page Friday, said the accident occurred Dec 15, but Codelco officials only allowed authorities onto the site 11 days later to carry out tests.

Around 13,000 liters of solution containing copper and acid leaked from a canal running alongside the heap-leaching piles and then flowed downhill to the River Loa which lies five kilometers away, according to the paper.

There are no signs of serious damage to plants and animals in the area as at the time of the accident the river had a relatively high water flow which diluted the acid, said acting regional governor Tomislav Ostoic.
"Fortunately, the acid solution leaked in moments when the river had a high volume of water...so that the concentration was quite diluted," Ostoic told El Mercurio.
Four workers died at the pit in October after a tunnel over a conveyor belt collapsed, crushing the men under tonnes of rocks and debris.
Chilean safety authorities criticized safety measures at the pit after last year's accident.
El Abra, which cast its first cathode in August, is designed to produce 225,000 tonnes of fine copper cathodes a year.
The pit uses the new, low-cost heap-leaching process which involves sprinkling sulphuric acid over the mineral ore to extract the copper, bypassing the traditional concentrator and smelter.
